Class ServerSetup

java.lang.Object
com.atomictempest.core.ServerSetup
public final class ServerSetup extends Object
The setup wizard (/tempest setup, API version 38): an admin picks what kind of server it is, and every Tempest plugin fits itself to it in one go: shop items and prices, crates, quests, daily rewards, mob coins. Each plugin registers a ServerSetup.Part that says what it would do, does it, and can take it back. 
core.setupPart(new ServerSetup.Part() {
    public String title() { return "Crates"; }
    public List<ServerSetup.Change> preview(ServerSetup.Kind kind) {
        return List.of(new ServerSetup.Change("farmer", "Adds the Farmer's Crate (200)"));
    }
    public List<String> apply(ServerSetup.Kind kind, Set<String> chosen) {   // the ids the admin kept ticked
        ...; return List.of("Added the Farmer's Crate");
    }
    public boolean canUndo() { ... }
    public List<String> undo() { ...; return List.of("Removed the Farmer's Crate"); }
});
Rules for a part: only add, never delete what the admin made; skip what is there already; keep to the free edition's limits; check every item id exists; remember what it added or changed, so ServerSetup.Part.undo() can take back exactly that. apply and undo run off the world thread (they save files).

The guards, so a setup never spoils a server that already has its own:

  • a setting the admin changed from how it comes starts unticked (ServerSetup.Change.ticked): only what is still the plugin's own default is changed unless the admin ticks it;
  • backup(String, Path...) before anything is written: the part's files are copied to setup-backups/<time>/;
  • undo takes back only what is still as the setup made it (fingerprint(Object)): something the admin edited since, or a crate placed in the world, stays;
  • one setup or undo at a time on the whole server (begin()), whichever admins press;
  • it opens by itself only on a new server, never after an update.
